_comment: Alabama 2027 Housing Credit QAP, AHFA, adopted 10 June 2026. Scoring is Addendum A, the Point Scoring System, PDF pp.34-46 (printed A-1 to A-13). The addendum is explicitly two-sided: Points Gained less Points Lost gives the project score. Page numbers are PDF page indices. Within-criterion detail that spans pages of definitions is summarised in notes rather than split into separate criteria.

track_totals.note: No maximum is stated overall. The two stated section maxima are Project Characteristics 84 and Applicant Characteristics 20. Honouring every stated subsection cap gives 101 rather than 104, because Rent Affordability's items total 13 against a stated 16. The operative figure is a floor: 'Projects with a net score of less than 70 points (Points Gained less Points Lost) will not be considered for allocation.' Deductions are open-ended: negative neighbourhood services, existing project non-compliance and post-inspection non-compliance are each marked No Maximum. AHFA also reserves the right to deny an allocation regardless of ranking, and to allocate irrespective of ranking order.

groups.label: New construction against rehabilitation component points
groups.source_quote: New Construction Projects Only (Maximum of 8 Points)
groups.note: A project is either new construction or rehabilitation, and each route caps at 8. Together with the 25-point amenities maximum this is what makes the stated Type of Construction maximum of 33.

groups.label: Tenant needs, capped at the subsection maximum
groups.note: The five tenant needs items total 6 points against a stated subsection maximum of 5, so a project cannot claim them all.

groups.label: Project type, capped at the subsection maximum
groups.note: The four project type items total 21 points against a stated subsection maximum of 12.

criteria.heading: Extra unit and project amenities
criteria.quote: A maximum of 25 points in aggregate will be given to projects that provide extra

tiers.tier_label: Camera or video monitoring of entries, parking and amenities
Lighting of all amenities, parking and entry and exit points
Unit security package, alarms on all entry doors and windows
Storm shelter meeting ICC-500 standards
Playground with commercial equipment and at least three activities
Outdoor fitness area with three equipment types
Covered picnic pavilion
Furnished children's activity or senior arts and crafts centre
Senior gathering area in multistorey elevator developments
Gazebo, minimum 16 by 16 feet
Computer centre with two or more computers, printer and internet
Splash centre of at least 500 square feet
Exercise or fitness room with three equipment types
Covered bus stop shelter
Storm doors, aluminium construction
Emergency pull cord or call button in each unit
Bike racks at the community building and an outdoor amenity area

criteria.note: Additive up to 25 in aggregate. The QAP specifies each amenity in physical detail, down to room sizes and equipment counts. Failing to deliver a represented amenity exposes the project and its responsible owners to point penalties and other sanctions.

criteria.heading: New construction: windows, doors and exterior materials
criteria.quote: 4 points will be given for storm windows; thermal break insulated windows

tiers.tier_label: Energy Star rated insulated windows and insulated exterior doors
Full brick, cementitious siding, stucco, cultured stone or CMU exterior

criteria.note: New construction only. The brick requirement is specified as at least 40% of each multifamily building façade from finished grade to eave line, or 50% for single-family, with entry areas included. No exterior insulation finishing system is acceptable.

criteria.heading: Rehabilitation: replacement of building components
criteria.quote: 2 points will be given for replacing all entry doors with insulated exterior doors

tiers.tier_label: Replace all entry doors and all windows, Energy Star rated
Replace all kitchen cabinets and countertops
Replace all plumbing fixtures
Further replacement item

criteria.note: Rehabilitation only, to a maximum of 8. Four 2-point replacement items; the fourth continues past the page break and is recorded generically rather than guessed at.

criteria.heading: Energy and water conservation and healthy living environment
criteria.quote: Energy/Water Conservation and Healthy Living Environment

tiers.tier_label: HVAC of 14.3 SEER2 or above
Energy Star cool roof shingles or metal roof with a 50-year warranty
Dehumidifiers in all units, controls inaccessible to tenants
Radiant barrier roof deck at all buildings
Kitchen range hood vented to the exterior with a damper
WaterSense labelled water closet, bathroom faucets and showerheads
Jumper ducts to closets without an HVAC duct
LED fixtures or bulbs at all interior and exterior unit fixtures
Humidistat controlled Energy Star ventilation fans in all bathrooms
Energy Star rated bath and kitchen exhaust fans

criteria.note: Ten measures worth 24 in total against an aggregate maximum of 8, so a project picks its best three or four.

criteria.heading: New funds committed to the project
criteria.quote: A maximum of 5 points in aggregate will be given to projects which

tiers.tier_label: Listed federal sources including AHP, non-AHFA HOME, USDA 515, CDBG or Choice Neighborhoods
Capital Fund Program, public housing sales proceeds or RAD, $30,001+ per unit
Capital Fund Program, public housing sales proceeds or RAD, $16,000-30,000 per unit

criteria.note: Funds must be permanent and newly committed, evidenced by a fully executed firm commitment; assumed or extended existing funds do not qualify. The first list scales by amount per unit as well, with 2 points at $4,000-8,000 per unit.

criteria.heading: Existing USDA 515 loan transfer
criteria.quote: A maximum of 3 points will be given to projects that have a letter from

tiers.tier_label: $30,001 or more per unit

criteria.note: Requires a USDA letter stating the applicant applied for transfer or assumption of an existing Rural Development 515 loan.

criteria.heading: Rental or operating subsidies
criteria.quote: A maximum of 2 points will be given to projects that have a commitment for rental/operating
criteria.note: From USDA Rural Development, HUD or a public housing authority, covering at least 25% of the proposed units.

criteria.heading: Forgoing the qualified contract option
criteria.quote: irrevocably commit in writing
criteria.note: An irrevocable written commitment not to request a qualified contract, remaining affordable through the full 30-year extended use period.

criteria.heading: Elderly set-aside
criteria.quote: 100% of the units in the project designed, equipped

criteria.heading: Low-income families with three-bedroom units
criteria.quote: with a minimum of 15% of the low-income units having three or more bedrooms
criteria.note: A 100% elderly election forfeits these points. Rehabilitation projects must already have the bedrooms.

criteria.heading: Set-aside for tenants with disabilities or homeless populations
criteria.quote: for tenants with disabilities or homeless populations for a minimum of 30

tiers.tier_label: At least 7% of total units, for 30 years
At least 5% of total units, for 30 years

criteria.note: Requires active marketing, a marketing and preference plan, and an executed Tenant Needs Memorandum of Understanding if funded. The population includes people fleeing domestic violence and those ageing out of foster care or leaving institutions.

criteria.heading: Targeting public housing waiting lists
criteria.quote: target  households on the public housing waiting lists

criteria.heading: Accessible units beyond the minimum
criteria.quote: 5% of the dwelling units be
criteria.note: At least 5% readily accessible to people with mobility impairments, plus a further 2% accessible to people with sensory impairments.

criteria.heading: Rehabilitation of a project with a maturing AHFA HOME loan
criteria.quote: for the rehabilitation of a project with an

tiers.tier_label: AHFA HOME loan repaid in full, principal and interest
Closed a 15-year extension of the original AHFA HOME loan

criteria.heading: Rehabilitation of a prior funded LIHTC project
criteria.quote: 5 points will be given for rehabilitation of a prior funded LIHTC project
criteria.note: Must be out of the 15-year compliance period and free of a current USDA 515 loan or pending transfer.

criteria.heading: Historic rehabilitation tax credit eligibility
criteria.quote: qualifies for the Alabama Historic Rehabilitation Tax Credit or Federal Historic Tax Credit

criteria.heading: Rehabilitation or replacement of existing multifamily housing
criteria.quote: Rehabilitation of existing multifamily residential rental housing
criteria.note: Also covers replacement of public housing authority multifamily housing, and replacement of housing destroyed or damaged in a presidentially declared disaster area. Demolished public housing counts if cleared within the last eight years.

criteria.heading: Neighbourhood services near the site
criteria.quote: 2 points will be given for each of the following neighborhood services located within

tiers.tier_label: Grocery store
Pharmacy or drug store
Convenience store
Bank or credit union
Hospital or doctor's office

criteria.note: Within 3 miles, or 5 miles in a USDA-defined rural area, measured by odometer from the site's automobile entrance to the service's car park entrance. Duplicate services do not count twice. Existing rural projects may submit the best available option for a grocery store. One point is deducted for each service AHFA cannot locate because of inaccurate directions.

criteria.heading: Adjacent to an incompatible use
criteria.quote: 5 points will be deducted for applications involving any other project that is
criteria.note: Marked No Maximum: there is no limit on points deducted for negative neighbourhood services. A prior-funded AHFA project at 85% occupancy loses 2 rather than 5. Adjacent means nearby, not necessarily touching. Fourteen incompatible uses are listed and the list is not exhaustive. No deduction for an adjacent railway if noise is under 65 dB outside and 45 dB inside, per the environmental report.

criteria.heading: Within 0.3 miles of an incompatible use
criteria.quote: 2 points will be deducted for applications involving any other project that is within .3 miles
criteria.note: Applies only where the project is not already adjacent to one. A prior-funded AHFA project at 85% occupancy loses 1 rather than 2. No deduction for a prison or jail co-located with a police station.

criteria.heading: Unsatisfactory streets and sidewalks
criteria.quote: 2 points will be deducted if the condition of the streets and sidewalks are
criteria.note: Street width and difficulty of access are taken into account.

criteria.heading: Participation of minorities or women
criteria.quote: A maximum of 5 points will be given to applicants with participation of minorities or
criteria.note: Either ownership in the ownership entity or a guarantee that at least 10% of total building cost goes to minority or women-owned businesses. The individual must be general partner, manager or managing member and hold at least 51% of the entity or participating business.

criteria.heading: Responsible owner development experience
criteria.quote: previous successful experience in the development of Active AHFA Projects
criteria.note: Projects with an AHFA reservation letter or HOME written agreement from 2000 or later; non-AHFA projects can also qualify, without duplication.

criteria.heading: Experienced managing agent
criteria.quote: 10 points will be given to applicants with sound, experienced managing agents
criteria.note: Measured by units or projects currently managed, with 10 points at 1,000 or more units or 10 or more projects. Only low-income units count, in projects at least 20% low income.

criteria.heading: Altering an approved project without consent
criteria.quote: altered an approved project in any manner different from
criteria.note: Marked No Maximum: 5 points for each occurrence, with no cap on the number of occurrences. Deductions cover non-compliance identified between 1 January and 31 December of the year before the QAP year, taking account of whether corrective action was completed by AHFA's deadline.

criteria.heading: Non-compliance after the initial on-site inspection
criteria.quote: Non-Compliance after the Initial On-Site Inspection
criteria.note: Marked No Maximum and no value is stated here: deductions follow Addendum B, the compliance monitoring procedures and penalty criteria, which is a separate document not extracted. Non-AHFA projects, in state or out, face the same requirements, except that Addendum B's 4-point threshold does not apply to them. points_max is left null because the addendum states no figure.

criteria.heading: Minimum net score of 70 points
criteria.quote: Projects with a net score of less than 70 points (Points Gained less Points Lost) will not be considered
criteria.note: AHFA also allocates generally to only one project per county, as a geographic balance priority.

criteria.heading: Least aggregate participation by a responsible owner
criteria.quote: the least amount of aggregate participation by any one
criteria.note: Aggregate participation counts all Housing Credit and HOME applications recommended for allocation in the current cycle.

criteria.quote: Estimated Tract Median Family Income from the Federal Financial Institutions

criteria.quote: the application located in a county with the least

criteria.heading: Public drawing
criteria.quote: priority will be given in accordance with a drawing
criteria.note: Nine tiebreakers in total; this extraction records the first four and the ninth, which are the ones legible without ambiguity in the text layer. The drawing is held the next business day in AHFA's boardroom, drawn by an impartial person, open to the public, with results posted on AHFA's website.
